questions.prompt: In OpenAI's Agents SDK, which guardrails always run after the agent completes?

options.text: Input guardrails, which run before the agent in blocking mode
options.explanation: Input guardrails can run before the agent (blocking) or alongside it (parallel).

options.text: Output guardrails, so they have no run_in_parallel option
options.explanation: Right. They check the final output, so the agent's work is already done.

options.text: None. Every guardrail can run in parallel with the agent
options.explanation: Output guardrails cannot. They need the finished output to check.

questions.prompt: What do the Claude docs suggest for pre-screening user input?

options.text: A lightweight model that returns a simple classification
options.explanation: Right. The docs use a small model and structured outputs to return a boolean such as is_harmful.

options.text: Only a regex list, because models cannot classify input
options.explanation: The docs list input validation for known patterns, and also use a model screen.

options.text: The main model, in the same long prompt as the task
options.explanation: Docs suggest a separate, lightweight screen before the input reaches the main conversation.

questions.prompt: What risk does the Gemini guide name for blocking with a static word list?

options.text: It makes every reply slower for all users of the app
options.explanation: The guide does not name speed. Its warning is about unintended blocking.

options.text: It can target a group that commonly uses words on the list
options.explanation: Right. The guide says a static blocklist can have unintended results like this.

options.text: It lets all rare words through without any check
options.explanation: A blocklist checks the words on it. The guide warns about who gets blocked.
